claims.text: Inherent lattice distortions in high-entropy alloys impede dislocation motion under cyclic dynamic loading.
Evolving short-range chemical order impedes dislocation motion under cyclic dynamic loading.
The combined effects of lattice distortion and short-range chemical ordering produce a dynamic balance of strength and ductility.
This mechanism gives high-entropy alloys greater strain-rate sensitivity than simpler, less chemically complex alloys.
Severe lattice distortions produced by multiple principal elements act as dislocation-pinning points.
Dynamic loading induces local chemical reordering.
Loading-induced local chemical reordering facilitates intermittent dislocation glide.
Pinning slows dislocation mobility and thereby increases strength.
Intermittent dislocation activity is sufficient to sustain ductility despite dislocation pinning.
Under dynamic loading, the high-entropy alloy will exhibit higher yield strength than the simpler-alloy baseline.
Under dynamic loading, the high-entropy alloy will exhibit improved ductility or energy absorption relative to the baseline.
The high-entropy alloy will show a measurable increase in strain-rate sensitivity relative to the baseline.
In-situ TEM will reveal dislocation interactions with regions having different degrees of chemical order.
Pronounced lattice distortions and evolving short-range order are absent from the proposed pure-Ni or simpler Ni-alloy baseline.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate in single-phase high-entropy alloys at moderate strain rates, room temperature, and inert conditions.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at cryogenic or ultra-high temperatures or in multiphase or highly segregated systems.

contradictions.description: Evolving short-range chemical order is first said to impede dislocation motion, whereas loading-induced local reordering is later said to facilitate dislocation glide. These effects could coexist, but the hypothesis does not distinguish the relevant ordering states or explain the directional change.
